summary: Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, Shimin Geng studied at Minzu University of China (~1949–1953), where he later held an academic post from approximately 1953 to 2000.

Shin Fujinaga is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested in 1991 and as Associate Professor in 2000), and at Hiroshima University (attested in 1992).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He served as professor at Hanazono University, Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and visited Harvard University in 1958.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University, founded the Kindai Pyramido Kyokai, and served as a professor at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested in 2015).

Shin'ya Yasutomi studied at Waseda University and earned a doctorate at Otani University. He worked in Buddhist studies, serving as a professor at Otani University (~1993–2010, 2014) and later directing the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute (~2010–2017).
Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served as a professor at Taisho University (~1957–1978) and later at Hanazono University (~1978–1986).

Shindo Kusumoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shingen Takagi, working in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Tohoku and Rissho universities under scholars including Kanakura, Hadano, Nakano, and Miyasaka. He held posts at Koyasan University, serving as assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995).

Shingo Einoo, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He served at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1985–1989), the University of Tokyo (~1989–2013), and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

Shinichi Nakazawa, working in religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977). He later held academic posts at Chuo University (~1993–2006), Tama Art University (~2006–2011), and Meiji University (~2011–2021).

Shinichi Tsuda studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and completed his Ph.D. at the Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham. He served at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2009).

Linguist Shinjiro Kazama studied at Hokkaido University (~1984–1994). He held an academic post at Tottori University (~1994–2007) before becoming a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2007.

Shinjo Hinonishi, an expert in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, where he was attested as assistant professor in 1980 and as professor in 2008.

Shinjo Kawasaki studied Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others. He held posts at the University at Buffalo, University of Tokyo, and served as professor at the University of Tsukuba (1975–1997).

Shinjo Suguro studied at the University of Tokyo, earning a doctorate in literature. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, he served as professor (~1971–1996) and professor emeritus (~1996–2004) at Rissho University.
Shinjosei Mochizuki worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at both the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University.
Shinkai Sugawara specialized in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and Taisho University, later serving as professor emeritus at Waseda University.

Shinkan Murakami studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano, earning his doctorate. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he was professor (~1974–1996) and professor emeritus at Tohoku University.

Shinko Nakai, working in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, studied at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1961–1965). He later served at Bukkyo University (~1978–2013) as a former president and professor emeritus.

Shinkō Mochizuki studied at Bukkyo, Taisho, and Tokyo universities under Tokuo Jonobe. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928), held multiple dean and professorial roles at Taisho University (~1926–1942), and became a Japan Academy member in 1947.
